content.text: {"label":"outage","explanation":"P2 incident INC-20261112-1271 opened at 11:58 says IMPS/NEFT transfers are stuck in pending. Accounts are debited but credits are not confirmed. In the same interval (11:45) payments volume jumped to 212 calls against 100 forecast (+112%). Service level fell to 4.7% with 81 calls abandoned. The rising reasons are payment_status_enquiry (1.64x normal) and refund_status (1.4x), which match the incident. Payments AHT is only modestly above forecast, and earlier intervals were near forecast, so this is not general system slowness. The KYC SMS at 10:50 would drive general-queue traffic, but general is below forecast, so it is not the cause. Payments has 4 sick absences against 2.4 usual, a small supply gap that explains the slight shortfall against planned agents but not the collapse. General is healthy (87-100% SL, volume below forecast).","plan_name":"IMPS outage containment for payments","rationale":"Cut avoidable demand first. A known-issue IVR message on payments covering the two rising reasons should stop about 20% of those callers. Chat deflection of payment and refund status enquiries removes more. Then add capacity. Move 8 cross-skilled agents from general, which is running under forecast at high SL; that is within the 30% cap of about 10-11 agents and should keep general above 70%. Delay payments breaks in the peak hour, cancel payments coaching through the afternoon, and run two consecutive overtime offers to cover 12:30-16:30. Overtime cost at about 40% acceptance is roughly 4 agents x 4 h x Rs 360 = Rs 5,760, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget. A callback is not added for now to avoid pushing work later while the outage may persist.
